I have 50 mu, and on that much land I do not play around too much. Wheat and maize are my full-year system, so I start from what worked on our side last year and then adjust a little for cost and water. I have done this 30 years, and around Quzhou most people who keep yield steady on wheat-maize do two things: they do not starve the crop, and they do not wait too long on water. I also watch fertilizer prices every year. If prices are high, I may trim a little, but I will not cut so much that the field goes hungry. Losing yield hurts more than spending a bit extra.

For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed. On my land, wheat needs a solid base fertilizer and then one topdressing when it turns green and starts pushing hard. I will put more nitrogen on wheat than on maize because wheat here responds clearly if water is there. Phosphorus I keep steady for rooting and tillering. Potassium I do use, but not as heavy as nitrogen. I have well irrigation, so I will give wheat about 3 waterings in a normal year: one after sowing if moisture is short, one at jointing, and one around grain filling if needed. For pests and disease, I will usually spray seed treatment plus 2 field sprays, mostly herbicide once and fungicide/insecticide once, sometimes combined. Tillage for wheat after maize, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is faster on 50 mu and easier to manage with family labor.

For summer maize, I will also use hybrid seed. Around here, if the stand is good and fertilizer is not short, hybrid maize pays. I do not push phosphorus as much as wheat, but I still put enough under the crop. Nitrogen I split, with some at sowing and the rest before the big growth stage, because maize eats hard in the middle. Potassium I keep at a fair level because if stalks are weak or ears do not fill well, that loss is real. With well water, I will plan 2 irrigations for maize in a normal season, one around jointing and one around tasseling-silking if rain does not come. For pesticides, I will usually do 2 applications, one herbicide early and one for insects if needed, especially if corn borer or armyworm pressure shows up. On maize after wheat, I prefer no-tillage or very light disturbance if the machine can place seed well, because it saves time in the tight summer window.
